didYouKnow.hook: Nobody actually knows how many 1st Edition Base Set cards were printed.
didYouKnow.body: The figure repeated everywhere is 10,000 copies of each card. It has never been confirmed by Wizards of the Coast or The Pokémon Company. It circulates as community lore, not documented fact.
didYouKnow.why_it_matters: So the next time someone quotes a print-run number at you as though it settles an argument, remember that the most repeated figure in the hobby has no source behind it.
sources: Fanatics Collect auction description (states the figure has never been confirmed)
didYouKnow.note: Published as an unconfirmed-claim story, never as a print-run figure. Single-source; framed accordingly.

sealedIndex.name: Catchem Sealed Index
sealedIndex.baseline: each product vs its first clean-history price (2026-08-18 cut)

valueWeighted.name: Catchem Sealed Index — value weighted
valueWeighted.simple: Same shelf, but the expensive boxes get a bigger say. If this number and the main one disagree, the cheap end and the expensive end of the market are moving differently.
valueWeighted.method: Each product's move is weighted by what it was worth at its baseline, so a $5,000 box counts for more than a $10 pack. The main index gives every product one equal vote.

sealedIndex.simple: One number for all 174 sealed products. 100 was the starting line; 100.8 means the whole shelf is worth more than when we started. Each product competes only against itself — one product, one vote.

rawIndex.name: Raw Chase Index
rawIndex.note: same equation as the Sealed Index — confirmed chase singles, each vs its own first clean price

model.buyerSide: delivered eBay total + sales tax (est. 7% — set your own in the app)
model.sellerSide: eBay ask minus 13.25% final value fee and $0.40 per order
model.note: Both figures are estimates from published fee schedules. A show price between them beats the online route for buyer and seller alike.
model.formula: buyerCeiling = ask × (1 + taxPct/100) · sellerFloor = ask × (1 − feePct/100) − feeFixed
